CHIEF COMPLAINT
Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 63-year-old female presenting for follow-up after mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. She was seen previously on 9/17 and was doing well from a cardiac standpoint at that time. Patient reports feeling better since surgery. She continues to experience some chest pain and shallow breathing with exertion, which resolves with activity modification and slowing down. Episodes last a few minutes and recur approximately once every couple of weeks, occurring a couple of times per month. Patient manages symptoms by taking the day slowly when they occur and avoiding pushing herself. She is compliant with medications using a reminder app. She denies new symptoms aside from the known chest discomfort and dyspnea with exertion. She notes initial irritability from atenolol which has since improved.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses exertional chest pain and dyspnea with exertion, both of which resolve with activity modification. Denies other symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Mitral regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, asthma, recurrent chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease, status post mitral valve repair 8/3/2020.

MEDICATIONS
Coumadin 4 milligrams, Lasix 4 milligrams daily, Atenolol 50 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well. Head and neck: No JVD detected. Lungs: Reduced breath sounds, auscultation and percussion clear. Heart: Rhythm irregularly irregular, S1 slightly accentuated, no S3 gallop. Abdomen: Non-tender. Extremities: Trace peripheral edema, non-tender feet.

RESULTS
ECG dated 12/26/2020 shows atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response and T-wave inversion anteriorly with no significant changes compared to previous study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient is recovering well from mitral valve repair surgery. Heart valves are working well. Atrial fibrillation is being well controlled on current medical regimen. Continue current medications: Coumadin 4 mg, Lasix 4 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily. Patient is encouraged to remain active as tolerated. Follow-up appointment in 6-9 months.
